audit_notes: Parameter check: a stack of SiO2/ZnS or SiO2/TiO2 layers with randomised thicknesses reflects broadband only when it has many layers (>20-30) with a thickness distribution spanning ~50-300 nm; single platelets of 1-2 um thickness are feasible (effect pigment technology). TiO2 and ZnS absorb the UV below 380/340 nm (~4-5 percent of solar), gaps between platelets and angle dependence lower the coating SR to ~0.88-0.90 new; aged 20-year mean ~0.84, so I raise the absorptance from 0.14 to 0.16. Emittance of the silicate binder ~0.92 (silica band near 9 um). Dimensionless: optical thickness per layer n*d/lambda ~ 0.25 at 0.5-1.5 um; Biot envelope 0.026. Simulation coefficient: sol-air excess (0.16*600-0.92*80)/20 = 1.12 K vs baseline 6.0 K. Model: steady 1D roof conduction, analytical. Baseline: aged cool paint alpha 0.32, eps 0.90. Expected gain ~26 percent (roof). Mechanical: platelet coatings are robust; specular sheen may cause glare on facades. Audit passed.
